title: Paving Plans, Power Prices, Jitney Rules Set
summary:
*   **New Street Paving & Utility Pricing:** City leaders ordered major street paving projects for Rio Grande and West 19th streets, including a direct contract for Rio Grande. They also set a new electric rate of 4 cents per kilowatt for heating purposes.
*   **Modern Transit Regulation (Jitneys):** Significant amendments were approved for the "jitney" (early shared taxi) ordinance, including allowing vehicle substitutions during breakdowns and modifying route length and permit revocation rules.
*   **Property Tax Adjustments & Flood Relief:** Multiple property tax assessments were corrected or reduced due to errors or "misunderstandings." Additionally, a tax penalty was waived for a resident who suffered severe losses in the 1915 floods.
*   **Community & Local Infrastructure:** Funds were allocated for new sanitary sewer construction, as well as the purchase of property and equipment for the East Austin Hose Co No 4 fire station.

The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Resolved by the City Council
of the City of Austin, Texas : That if the proponents of what is known as the Jitney
regulatory ordinance ,as hereto-fore presented by the firm of Hart, Patterson & Brownlee
of this City,and chieflyadvoca- Jitneys. -ted by Ben M Parker, W B Calloway and G M
Wagner,will so request in writing of the City Ordinance Council ,the City Council will
amend its present Jitney regulatory ordinance in the following particulars: 1. We will
make the permits to expirewith the current year ,beginning with the date of their
respective several issuances.
2. We woll modify the phraseoligy of the ordinance so that in the event of a Break-down or
other misfortune to any car ,another car can be substituted under the same license until
repairs are made .
3. We will change that provision of the ordinance which gives the City Council the right
to revoke in its descretion any permit establishing a route,and substitute therefor the
right only to revoke such permit as to routes for good and suffcicient causes.
4. We will change the length of the routes in any givrn direction,from terminus to
terminus ,from thirty fivr (35) blocks as is the present requirement of the ordinance, to
thirty (30) blocks where the routes start and end on this side of the Colorado river, and
we will make the length of the routes 20 blocks where the routes begin and end , either on
the south side of the Colorado river or cover a route partly on the south side of the
Colorado river and partly on the north side of the Colorado river.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.

The Council then adjourned.
